title: Alignment Incident
description: One incident of an AI system behaving contrary to the intent of its developers, deployers, or users. One file per incident in data/incidents/<id>.yaml.

id.description: Stable slug, must equal the filename without .yaml. Format: YYYY-MM-short-kebab-name. Never change once published.

title.description: Neutral, factual headline. Avoid sensational language.

date.description: When the behavior occurred, or was first publicly reported if the occurrence date is unknown. Use only the precision you can source: YYYY, YYYY-MM, or YYYY-MM-DD. Quote it in YAML.

status.description: confirmed: acknowledged by the developer/deployer, or documented in primary research with methodology. reported: credible public reports but no confirmation. disputed: credible sources contest the account. retracted: shown to be false; kept for the record.

setting.description: Where the behavior happened. deployment: real users / real stakes in a shipped product. evaluation: a developer's or third party's pre/post-release testing (system cards, evals). research: a constructed experiment designed to study the behavior. red-team: adversarial elicitation (jailbreaks, prompt injection) by testers.

harm.description: Real-world harm that actually occurred (not hypothetical). none: no real-world harm (typical for research/eval). minor: inconvenience, embarrassment, small recoverable losses. moderate: significant financial, data, or reputational damage, or harm to individuals that was recoverable. severe: serious injury, death, or large irreversible losses.

models.description: Model ids from data/taxonomy/models.yaml. Use 'unknown' if the model is not disclosed.

organizations.description: Organizations involved, each with a role. ids from data/taxonomy/organizations.yaml.

role.description: developer: built the model. deployer: shipped the product where it happened. researcher: ran the study/eval that found it. reporter: first publicly reported it. affected: harmed by it.

behaviors.description: Behavior ids from data/taxonomy/behaviors.yaml. List the most central behavior first.

summary.description: 2-5 sentence neutral overview, plain text. Every fact in it must also appear in `claims` with a source.

claims.description: Atomic factual statements, each backed by one or more sources. This is the evidentiary core of the record.

sources.description: Source ids from this file's `sources` list.

quote.description: Optional short verbatim quote from the source supporting the claim.

id.description: Short local id, unique within this file.

kind.description: primary: from the developer/deployer or the person who experienced it. research: paper, system card, or research write-up with methodology. news: journalism. social: social media post. analysis: commentary/blog analysis.

tags.description: Free-form tags for things not covered by the taxonomies (e.g. agentic, coding-agent, system-card).

review_status.description: draft: not yet checked by a human against sources. reviewed: a maintainer verified every claim against its sources.
